subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction wake and execution semantics use the shared notificationWake.reactions policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611, a Telegram-specific reaction semantics API, or separate narrower follow-ups before implementation?
rationale: Current main only has passive reaction system events, and the missing behavior adds public wake/config semantics that affect channel delivery and session timing, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Adopt Shared Opt-In Wake Policy
options.body: Use a queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical default-safe wake path, then leave per-emoji execution and durability to narrower follow-ups.

options.title: Sponsor Telegram-Specific Semantics
options.body: Choose a Telegram reactionSemantics-style API and require schema, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof for the added config surface.

options.title: Keep The Work Split
options.body: Keep this issue as the Telegram umbrella while the cross-channel wake, prompt guidance, custom emoji, and durable persistence pieces land independently.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Opt-In Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use a queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical default-safe wake path, then leave per-emoji execution and durability to narrower follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the open shared-policy candidate and has the strongest current evidence for choosing the public config/API direction.
